data.name: Designer.Help.GlobalScoreRow.Content
data.value:
GlobalScoreRow is a parent score-row frame. Its cells are fixed internal score cells: they cannot be deleted and they are not global layers.
After selecting the parent row, choose a child in the dedicated Score Cells list; while a child is selected, SelectedDesignItem remains the parent row.
Visibility controls whether each cell is shown, hidden, or collapsed in the current Canvas state; BO3 and BO5 states own independent row and cell layouts.
Auto Arrange by Spacing uses MajorGameGap / HalfGameGap to arrange the visible sequence for the current state, then each cell can be fine-tuned manually.
Apply Parent Style to All Cells copies the parent font family, weight, color, size, and camp icon settings into all child overrides; blank style fields inherit from the parent.

data.name: Designer.Help.BackgroundTint.Content
data.value:
BackgroundTintRectangle and BackgroundTintPolygon automatically use the effective Canvas background; no duplicate image selection is needed.
They generate an aligned static tinted copy and clip it to the rectangle or polygon, preserving the background texture.
BaseColorWithTexture treats TintColor as the target base color and TextureStrength controls the visible source detail; LuminanceColorize and Multiply keep their existing darker behavior.
TintBindingPath can bind to HomeTeam.ColorHex or AwayTeam.ColorHex and regenerates when the team color changes.
This uses occasional CPU regeneration, not real-time GPU blending.

data.name: Designer.Graph.Help.Concepts.Content
data.value:
The node graph editor is a visual tool for composing control animations. Each graph consists of nodes and connections.
Nodes represent actions (e.g. set a property, play an animation); connections define execution order.
A graph starts at the Start node and ends at an End node.

Nodes fall into three categories: flow control nodes (control execution order), action nodes (manipulate control properties), and value nodes (provide constant data).

data.name: Designer.Graph.Help.Workflow.Content
data.value:
Drag nodes from the catalog on the left onto the canvas, or double-click a catalog item to quickly add it.
Drag from a node's output port (blue marker on the right) to another node's input port (marker on the left) to create a connection.
Click a node card to select it; the property panel on the right shows editable properties.
Press Delete to remove the selected node or connection. Use the toolbar buttons to duplicate a node or auto-create Start/End nodes.
Type keywords in the catalog search box to quickly find node types.

data.name: Designer.Graph.Help.NodeTypes.Content
data.value:
Flow Control Nodes:
Start — Entry point; each graph must have exactly one.
End — The single graph ending point; multiple branches can connect to the same End.In.
Delay — Waits for the specified number of milliseconds.
Sequence — Runs Step1 → Step2 → Step3 in order.
Parallel — Runs Branch1, Branch2, Branch3 simultaneously; continues when all complete.
If — Text comparison branch. Compares Left and Right, goes to True on match, False otherwise.

Action Nodes:
Log — Writes a line to the execution log for debugging.
SetProperty — Sets a control property value, e.g. Target=Self, PropertyName=Opacity, Value=0.5.
ResetProperty — Resets a control property. Use a specific property name or All.
AnimateProperty — Sends a property animation to the target control. Fill in PropertyName, From, To, DurationMs and Easing.

Value Nodes:
Number / String / Boolean / Color — Constant value nodes, editable in the property panel.
ControlReference — Target control reference; Self means the control this behavior is bound to.

data.name: Designer.Graph.Help.Preview.Content
data.value:
Make sure the graph has one Start node and one End node.
Click Run Preview in the toolbar to execute the current graph. The animation runs on the real controls in the designer and is shown live in the preview viewport (bottom-left).
The execution log (bottom-right) shows the result of each step, helping you troubleshoot.
Click Stop Preview to interrupt execution. Use Reset Current Target or Reset All Preview to restore modified control properties.
The preview viewport uses real-time rendering so you can see animation effects directly.

data.name: Designer.Graph.Help.LoopPreview.Content
data.value:
Loop behaviors have three stage graphs: Start Graph, Loop Graph, and End Graph.

Preview one loop animation: runs Start Graph → runs Loop Graph once → runs End Graph.
Start loop animation preview: runs the Loop Graph repeatedly (controlled by RepeatCount and IntervalMs) until you click Stop loop animation preview.
Preview stop animation: runs only the End Graph so you can check the stop-stage effect.
Reset preview: restores all control properties modified by preview.

RepeatCount controls the number of loops; use a negative value for infinite looping until manually stopped. IntervalMs controls the wait time between loops; when it is 0, preview still keeps a short UI-friendly tick to avoid freezing the editor.

data.name: Designer.Graph.Help.Troubleshooting.Content
data.value:
Preview does not run: check for a Start node, verify all nodes are connected, and look for validation errors.
Animation effect is unexpected: check AnimateProperty's From/To values and DurationMs, and verify the easing function.
Cannot connect nodes: make sure output port type (Flow/Value) matches input port type. Flow ports only connect to Flow ports; Value ports only connect to Value ports.
Graph execution hangs: check if a Delay node has an extremely large duration, or if all Parallel branches have End nodes.
Control animation has no effect: check that Target is correct (commonly Self) and PropertyName is spelled correctly (e.g. Opacity, Width, Height).

data.name: Designer.Graph.Help.Content
data.value: This editor only edits the property animation flow that runs after a behavior is triggered. Configure events, triggers, and filters in the behavior panel. Basics: drag nodes from the catalog onto the canvas; drag a node header to move it; drag from an output port to an input port to connect; use the × button on a connection to disconnect; drag empty canvas space with the left or right mouse button to pan; select a node and edit its properties on the right; right-click a node or press Delete to remove it. Flow nodes: Start is the entry point and a graph should normally have one. End is the single ending point, and multiple branches can connect to End.In. Delay waits for a number of milliseconds. Sequence runs Step1, Step2, Step3 in order. Parallel runs Branch1, Branch2, Branch3 together and waits for all of them. If is an advanced text branch and is usually not needed for simple property animation. Action nodes: Log writes preview text. SetProperty writes a property value, for example Target=Self, PropertyName=Opacity, Value=0.5. ResetProperty resets a property; PropertyName can be a specific property or All. AnimateProperty plays a property animation, for example Target=Self, PropertyName=Opacity, From=0, To=1, DurationMs=300, Easing=Linear. In preview, these actions are applied to the designer preview controls when a target scope is available. Value nodes: Number/String/Boolean/Color store constant values for later value-port evaluation. ControlReference stores a target reference; Self is the common value today.
